# gtropic <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="145" alt="" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![License: GPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPLv3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0)
<!-- badges: end -->

`gtropic` retrieves, filters and maps tropical cyclone exposure data from
G-TROPIC, a collection published on Harvard Dataverse and updated weekly. It
holds wind, precipitation and flood exposure for every second-level
administrative unit (ADM2) worldwide and every storm in the International Best
Track Archive for Climate Stewardship (IBTrACS) since 1980. The package returns
the published values as they are and recomputes nothing.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("sparklabnyc/gtropic")
```

## Example

Find Hurricane Katrina, retrieve the wind exposure it caused, and map it:

```{r katrina-retrieve, message = FALSE}
library(gtropic)

katrina_id <- gtropic_storms(STORM_NAME = "Katrina-2005")$STORM_ID
katrina <- gtropic_data(
  STORM_ID = katrina_id,
  date_range = 2005,
  tables = c("wind", "tracks", "adm2", "geometry")
)
```

```{r katrina-print}
katrina
```

```{r katrina-map, fig.alt = "Map of the eastern United States, Cuba and the Bahamas in which each administrative unit is shaded by the maximum sustained wind it received from Hurricane Katrina in August 2005, with the storm's track drawn on top and coloured by Saffir-Simpson category."}
gtropic_plot(katrina)
```

A storm name such as `"Katrina-2005"` can match more than one storm, so look it
up with `gtropic_storms()` and query by the unique `STORM_ID`.

Every result carries a manifest of the exact files it used. Saved as JSON, it
replays the same retrieval later, even after the dataset has been revised:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
gtropic_manifest_write(katrina, path)
gtropic_data(manifest = gtropic_manifest_read(path))
```

## Main functions

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `gtropic_storms()`, `gtropic_adm2()` | Look up storms and administrative units |
| `gtropic_data()` | Retrieve exposure tables for chosen storms, places and dates |
| `gtropic_plot()` | Draw static or interactive maps of a result |
| `gtropic_manifest_write()`, `gtropic_manifest_read()` | Save a retrieval and replay it |
| `gtropic_cache_list()`, `gtropic_cache_prune()` | Inspect and tidy the download cache |

## Learn more

- [Getting started](https://sparklabnyc.github.io/gtropic/articles/getting-started.html): a first query and what it returns.
- [Filtering](https://sparklabnyc.github.io/gtropic/articles/filtering.html): how place, date and storm filters combine.
- [Linkage](https://sparklabnyc.github.io/gtropic/articles/linkage.html): joining precipitation and flood records to storms without double counting.
- [Plotting](https://sparklabnyc.github.io/gtropic/articles/plotting.html): static and interactive maps.
- [Versions and caching](https://sparklabnyc.github.io/gtropic/articles/versions-and-caching.html): reproducible retrieval and the download cache.

## Citation

Please cite both the package and the G-TROPIC datasets. The dataset DOIs and
versions behind a result are listed by `gtropic_manifest()`.
